newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine 91-day dlr bills sale seen at 6-6.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Argentine 91-day dlr bills sale seen at 6-6.5 pct.

text.p: Analysts said Argentina's placement of $250 million 91-day Treasury bills (Letes) on Tuesday is likely to fetch a cut off yield between 6.0 and 6.5 percent.
The issue is seen well bid particularly because of the surge in debt markets in recent sessions.
"Considering how strong the debt markets have been, I think the issue will fetch a much higher price than last month," said Cristina Gintz, an analyst at Banco de la Provincia de Buenos Aires.
Last month's auction of 182-day dollar bills attained a cut-off yield of 6.49 percent.
But analysts and traders noted that the expected drop in rates will be less significant to local markets because these Letes are dollar-denominated and not in pesos.
"It is not going to indicate a lot of anything," said a bond analyst at a large foreign bank, pointing to the fact that it is a dollar issue.

One of the most important indicators in Argentina of country risk is the spread between peso and dollar assets, and analysts say the outcome of a dollar issue will not have the importance for the market that the peso auctions have in previous months.
The monthly peso issues have offered the markets comparisons to judge the fluctuations in short-term risk.
But either way, dollar-denominated instruments have rallied sharply in recent sessions and there is little doubt this issue will be well bid, said traders.
The 91-day peso-denominated bills sold last month got a cut-off yield of 8.50 percent. At July's sale of 91-day peso bills there was a cut-off yield of 6.86 percent.

Economy Ministry officials said the size of the issue this month is only $250 million because the debt ceiling set for the year has nearly been reached. Separately, the official said the issue is in dollars because of the large spread between peso and dollar rates.
Offers are due by 1400 local time/1700 GMT. The sale is offered in Dutch auction with settlement due on September 20.
